transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-05-06 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Head of Platform, Asterion), Liam O'Connor (Security Engineer), Jamal Reed (CTO)

Summary:
Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for inference. Primary concerns: SOC2/ISO artifacts, SSO/SAML & SCIM, RBAC model, audit logging retention and export, encryption/KMS with customer-managed keys, data residency and retention policies. Wants clear checklist for procurement and a technical deep-dive for Dedicated/VPC + KMS.

Topics Covered:
- Compliance artifacts (SOC2 Type II, ISO27001)
- SSO (SAML) and SCIM provisioning
- RBAC and least privilege for model API keys
- Audit logs, retention windows, immutable exports
- Encryption options: Redwood-managed KMS vs customer-managed CMKs/HSM
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (tradeoffs on latency, cost, isolation)

Action items (captured during call):
- Maya to send SOC2 report + security pack link
- Diego to draft Dedicated/VPC network diagram and KMS integration notes
- Asterion (Liam) to share retention policy and compliance questionnaire answers

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood. Um, we also have Diego, our solutions engineer, on the line. How are you all?
[00:07] Priya Patel: Good, thanks. We appreciate you making time. We wanted to start broadly — we're about to kick off procurement for a vendor to handle our inference layer for routing and embeddings — so we need to validate security posture.
[00:18] Jamal Reed: Yeah, and speed is important too, but security is gating for us. We need to understand your SOC2, ISO status, and what options we have for KMS and VPC deployment.
[00:28] Diego Alvarez: Sure, totally. Quick intro, I'm Diego, I work on infra and deployment for Redwood. Happy to walk through both the compliance artifacts and how we'd integrate with your key management.
[00:36] Liam O'Connor: Cool. A couple specifics up front — do you have a SOC2 Type II report we can share with our auditors? Also ISO 27001?
[00:45] Maya Chen: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and an ongoing ISO program. I'll share our latest SOC2 Type II artifact; ISO attestation is in progress but we have the audit plan and gap remediation notes.
[00:55] Priya Patel: Great. On authentication — we use Okta and SAML single sign-on. We also push users via SCIM. Can Redwood integrate with SAML + SCIM and provide RBAC tied to our groups?
[01:05] Diego Alvarez: Yep. We support SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning. Our Console can sync groups and map to roles — you can tie Okta groups to Redwood roles like Admin, Operator, Viewer. There's some nuance on token-level usage for API calls — we surface token-level audit logs.
[01:20] Liam O'Connor: When you say token-level logs, is that per API key — full request/response metadata or just metadata? We can't store PII in logs.
[01:28] Diego Alvarez: Good Q. By default audit logs capture request metadata — timestamp, calling principal, model id, model version, token counts, latency, and a hashed request id. We do not store full raw customer inputs in plain text in the audit index. There's an opt-in for storing request payloads for debugging, which we recommend only for short windows and with encryption.
[01:45] Priya Patel: What is the retention on those logs? Our legal team requires seven years for certain audit trails.
[01:52] Maya Chen: Out of the box we retain operational logs for 90 days in the Console and have exports to a customer-owned S3 or GCS bucket for long-term archival. For Hosted customers we can push logs to your cloud and you can manage long-term retention. Dedicated/private gives more control.
[02:10] Jamal Reed: So for hosted, Redwood manages the storage but you can configure a push to our bucket?
[02:15] Diego Alvarez: Exactly. We can stream audit logs to a customer-owned storage endpoint; we also support encrypted delivery to that bucket. For Dedicated and Private, customers often keep logs inside their VPC or on-prem storage so retention and access controls are fully theirs.
[02:28] Liam O'Connor: Regarding encryption — we need CMK support. Can we bring our own key and rotate it? HSM?
[02:35] Diego Alvarez: Yes. For Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed keys — you can bring CMKs (KMS) and in some Private deployments connect to on-prem HSMs via an approved connector. For Hosted, we offer Redwood-managed KMS with an option for customer-managed CMKs via cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS) where we accept encrypted envelopes; in practice it's a bit more involved and we can show the architecture.
[02:55] Priya Patel: That architecture doc would be helpful. We need a clear flow: request leaves our app, hits Redwood, how are keys used, do you re-encrypt, where are tokens cached?
[03:05] Diego Alvarez: We'll produce a diagram. Important distinction: the inference runtime maintains an in-memory KV cache for model state; that is ephemeral and never written to disk. The persistent artifacts — model weights are read-only and encrypted at rest. Request/response payloads are not persisted unless you opt-in for debugging exports, and all persisted objects can be encrypted with your CMK in Dedicated/Private.
[03:24] Priya Patel: You mentioned KV cache — we had it transcribed as like K V cache earlier in the doc, but ok. On RBAC, can we define granular permissions for service accounts and user groups? We need least-privilege for production keys and separate staging keys.
[03:36] Maya Chen: Yes — the Console supports role-based access controls, and you can mint scoped API keys with route- and model-level permissions. We also support short-lived keys and can attach session policies and scopes. We'll share examples of policies.
[03:47] Liam O'Connor: Audit logs need to show who rotated keys and when. Does the audit include key management operations?
[03:53] Diego Alvarez: Yes, key management ops such as key creation, rotation events, and access attempts are logged. Those events are included in the audit stream and can be exported to your SIEM (we've done Splunk, Datadog, and SumoLogic integrations).
[04:05] Jamal Reed: Does Redwood have attestation for role separation? Our compliance requires that operators cannot access raw request content.
[04:12] Maya Chen: Separation of duties is a core part of our controls — operator consoles are RBAC-limited and access to sensitive payloads is gated and logged. For Dedicated and Private we can enforce stricter network and SSO controls, and for Hosted we have internal controls documented in the SOC2.
[04:25] Priya Patel: On SOC2 — does your SOC2 Type II cover both the hosted API and the control plane for Dedicated?
[04:31] Maya Chen: The SOC2 covers our hosted control plane and managed services. For Dedicated we provide a baseline set of controls and can supply architecture and control mappings. Some customers require us to supply a dedicated control attestation or coordinate an audit scope — we've supported that via our enterprise team.
[04:44] Liam O'Connor: Ok. Data residency — our EU customers' data must stay in EU regions. How granular is region pinning?
[04:50] Diego Alvarez: You can pin model serving to region pools. Hosted supports region selection for customer data and serving. Dedicated provides region-level isolation and Private/on-prem obviously stays where you put it. We'll include region pinning options in the checklist.
[05:03] Priya Patel: About procurement — our legal team wants to see encryption-in-transit specs, cipher suites, mutual TLS, and key rotation cadence.
[05:11] Maya Chen: We use TLS1.2/1.3, mTLS for internal service-to-service in Dedicated, and for customer-facing endpoints TLS termination is enforced. Key rotation cadence is flexible — for CMKs you control rotation when you supply CMKs; otherwise we rotate platform keys on a schedule and it is documented in the security pack.
[05:27] Jamal Reed: Any known limitations for private deployments around model updates or rollouts? Our ops team worries about rollback strategy.
[05:34] Diego Alvarez: For Private we ship a control plane that can manage rollouts; model updates can be staged with canary policies. The runtime supports automatic fallback to pinned model variants if new model fails. Rollback is automated via the Console or can be invoked via API. There is an ops checklist for Private upgrades that we can share.
[05:50] Liam O'Connor: Are there features to scrub PII from logs before they land in our archive?
[05:55] Diego Alvarez: We have redaction and hash-based pseudonymization hooks you can enable on the export path so PII is replaced or hashed before export. Typically customers run a privacy filter in their ingestion pipeline as well.
[06:06] Priya Patel: Ok thinking of risks — what are the main security trade-offs between Hosted and Dedicated?
[06:11] Maya Chen: Hosted is fastest to onboard, lower overhead, and Redwood manages the control plane and infra, but you rely on our operational controls and need to trust log export to your bucket for long-term retention. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity, VPC isolation, and customer-managed keys — more control but higher cost and slightly more ops. Private/on-prem is full isolation for highly regulated workloads but adds integration work and longer lead time.
[06:33] Jamal Reed: Do you support SAML for API clients or just the UI sessions?
[06:38] Diego Alvarez: SAML is primarily for UI SSO. For API clients you generally use scoped API keys or short-lived tokens minted via the SSO provider using an OIDC flow. We support OIDC token exchange for automation as well.
[06:50] Liam O'Connor: On the short-lived tokens — what max TTLs can you issue?
[06:54] Diego Alvarez: We support TTLs down to minutes and up to a few hours; for longer lived credentials we recommend scoped API keys with rotation. We'll include recommended TTLs based on your risk profile in the follow-up.
[07:06] Priya Patel: Can you confirm the encryption-at-rest algorithms and if you support customer-supplied KMS keys in GCP and Azure or only AWS?
[07:14] Maya Chen: We support CMKs in AWS KMS and GCP KMS in Dedicated/Private; Azure is on the roadmap and we've done customer-specific integrations before. Algo-wise, AES-256 for disk encryption and envelope encryption for object storage; the exact cipher suites are in the security pack.
[07:29] Jamal Reed: Do you provide an artifact mapping that aligns your controls to our SOC2/ISO questionnaire?
[07:34] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll include a controls matrix mapping Redwood controls to common frameworks. That's part of the security pack we share with prospective enterprise customers.
[07:44] Priya Patel: Ok let's talk about procurement timeline — we aim to decide vendor by end of Q2, so about 6 weeks. We'll need your SOC2, a VPC checklist, and a deep-dive technical session.
[07:55] Maya Chen: Sounds good. We'll prioritize sending SOC2 artifacts today and schedule the deep-dive. Diego — can you lead the technical deep-dive next week?
[08:02] Diego Alvarez: Yep, I can. I'll coordinate with Liam and schedule a 60-minute session for architecture and KMS details.
[08:09] Liam O'Connor: Perfect. I also want to run a short perf baseline for latency — are you able to provide a simple benchmarking harness for us to run against Hosted and Dedicated?
[08:18] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we have a small benchmark script and a guidance doc for egress/ingress tuning, batch settings and quantization recommendations. We'll attach that. For Dedicated the baseline will be different because of reserved pools.
[08:32] Priya Patel: Any dependencies for Dedicated? Like VPC peering, egress rules? We want a checklist.
[08:37] Diego Alvarez: There's a VPC deployment checklist — it includes VPC peering, route table settings, NAT vs egress gateway, firewall rules for ports, and the KMS networking requirements. We'll include sample CloudFormation/Terraform snippets.
[08:51] Jamal Reed: On governance, do you support audit log immutability? Our compliance needs append-only logs for certain events.
[08:58] Maya Chen: For exports to customer buckets you can apply object lock / WORM policies on S3/GCS. We also support streaming logs to your SIEM where you can enforce immutability.
[09:09] Priya Patel: Ok, last question for now — what's your incident response SLAs and notification process for security incidents?
[09:15] Maya Chen: We have an IR playbook; for enterprise customers we provide a P1/P2 notification cadence and a dedicated contact. We'll include an excerpt in the pack and can provide the full playbook under NDA if needed.
[09:27] Liam O'Connor: Good. That should cover our initial compliance gating.
[09:31] Maya Chen: To recap next steps: I'll send the SOC2 Type II report and security pack; Diego will prepare Dedicated/VPC diagram, KMS notes, and benchmarking harness; Liam will send Asterion retention policy and specific compliance questions. We'll schedule the deep-dive for 2026-05-13.
[09:46] Jamal Reed: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:49] Priya Patel: Thanks — appreciate it.
